clue.text: D Trump's most influential supporter snubbed victors in Australian war

indicators.note: a snub nose is a short one, so snubbed means cut short at the end

parts.note: the billionaire Elon Musk, written with his initial

explanation.surface: A top Trump backer gets cold-shouldered, with a nod to some forgotten Australian conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter of E MUSK. In the 1932 Emu War, Australian soldiers with machine guns failed to cull the birds, who are therefore called its winners.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless birds famously outlasted an army campaign in Western Australia, so history credits them with victory.

clue.text: Notice Mike Pence, perhaps, providing guidance

parts.note: a notice in a paper is an advertisement, shortened
Pence was Trump's vice president; 'perhaps' marks him as one example

explanation.surface: An observation about Trump's deputy offering counsel to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is counsel or recommendations, which is exactly what guidance offers.

clue.text: Second best for the most part, rugby player is getting in a row

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is kept, so its final letter goes

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
best and top both mean finest
the backs are the rugby players behind the scrum

explanation.surface: A rugby player who mostly finishes runner-up is drawn into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a fight to match the rugby picture, but it means a line or sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that happen back-to-back come one straight after another, consecutively, as in a row.

clue.text: Prevents American former soldiers arresting Republican

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to take hold of them, so these letters close around another

explanation.surface: US ex-servicemen detain a Republican politician to stop something happening.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to ward it off, so averts is a synonym of prevents.

clue.text: Chasing girls, primarily, the Parisian pulls — but they're worn out

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so the later words come after this one
primarily points to what comes first, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: to drag is to pull along

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who chases women gets lucky, though he ends up exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' suggests exhausted, but it means worn when going out.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags are one's best party clothes, put on for an evening out.

clue.text: Place to leave complaint, and make another

indicators.note: the abbreviation is told to go away, so it is removed from the longer word

parts.note: a plague is a disease; complaint can mean illness
standard abbreviation, as in street names

explanation.surface: Somewhere you go to lodge a grievance, then lodge a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: Complaint here means an illness, not a grievance: PLAGUE without PL leaves AGUE, a second illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a malarial fever with shivering fits, so it is a further ailment.

clue.text: Leader to remain in touch to get commission

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the following word

parts.note: being in touch is being in contact

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

explanation.surface: A boss stays in communication in order to earn a sales commission.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a job given to someone by formal agreement, which is a contract.

clue.text: Hold bishop's attention

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Keep a churchman listening to you.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a weight is to hold or carry it up.

clue.text: Primitive means of communication evaluated: more than half is wasted

indicators.note: over half the letters are thrown away, so only the opening portion survives

explanation.surface: Someone assessing crude communication methods says most of the effort was squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: Five of the nine letters of EVALUATED go, leaving EVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediaeval, of the Middle Ages, is used loosely to mean backward or crude, like primitive.

clue.text: Fondle German guy?

parts.note: a guy is a rope holding a tent steady

explanation.walkthrough: Guy looks like a man, but it is the tent rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To grope someone is to fondle or paw them clumsily.

clue.text: Abuse staff

definitions.meaning: first meaning: criticism or verbal ill-treatment
second meaning: a walking pole or rod

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mistreating employees; staff is a rod, and abuse is the harsh criticism called stick in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting stick means being criticised, and a stick is also a long piece of wood like a staff.

clue.text: Marxist compiler is a bounder

parts.note: a crossword compiler is its setter

explanation.surface: A left-wing crossword maker is accused of being a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: Bounder looks like an old word for a rogue, but it means something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter is an Irish gun dog famous for bounding energetically about.

clue.text: Aromatic alcohols of pH 1 turned emulsive, essentially

indicators.note: turned round means the word is read from end to start
the essence of a word is its core, so its central letters are taken

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on alcohols at strong acidity becoming milky.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenols are compounds with a hydroxyl group on a benzene ring, a class of aromatic alcohols.

clue.text: Chooses guitar players

definitions.meaning: second meaning: plectrums, the things a guitar is played with

explanation.walkthrough: Guitar players look like guitarists; they are the small plastic plectrums.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to select, and a pick is the plectrum used to strum a guitar's strings.

clue.text: Pacify primate eating vegetables

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater

explanation.surface: Calm down a monkey by feeding it greens.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to calm or placate them by giving way to demands.

clue.text: Twerp at riot is maybe displaying 'national pride'

indicators.note: the letters are on show within the run of words before it

parts.note: spans the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: An idiot causing trouble at a disturbance may be showing nationalistic fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriotism is love of and devotion to one's country.

clue.text: TV awards in balance? Try going climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read from bottom to top
the word before it departs, so its letters are removed

explanation.surface: A query about prizes hanging in the balance, with someone urged to have a go at climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmys are the main American television industry prizes.

clue.text: Clown around, at first, to get drink

parts.note: Coco the Clown, a famous circus clown

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is the part wanted

explanation.surface: A clown fools around and is rewarded with a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Around looks like a container signal; it is only the source of A. Coco was a celebrated Russian-born clown in British circuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot drink made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: Eucalyptus bush, one seen in trendy pub

explanation.surface: A shrub spotted in a fashionable drinking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen in' looks like a container signal, but the parts simply line up.
explanation.definitionFit: The coolibah or coolibar is an Australian eucalyptus tree of the outback.

clue.text: Gallium, sulphur or helium, perhaps?

explanation.surface: A chemistry question: which of these three elements is meant?
explanation.walkthrough: All three look like a list of elements; the first two give symbols and only helium is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is an example of a gas, a substance with no fixed shape at room temperature.

clue.text: Good to stop fishes making noises in the throat

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this letter sits inside the words after it

parts.note: two fishes: the gar and the ling

explanation.surface: It is a good thing to halt the fish who are croaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargling is bubbling liquid in the throat, which makes a rough throaty sound.

clue.text: Gathered together with the aim of blocking repellent symbol

indicators.note: a block stands in front of something, so this part comes before the other
to repel is to drive back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: People assembled with the purpose of obstructing an offensive emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or creature adopted as the emblem of a clan.

clue.text: Snore terribly, receiving fine, in game

indicators.note: the word takes the next one inside it
something done terribly is done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone snoring loudly in a match is fined for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters SNOER are split to take OK after their third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue game played on a large baize table with red and coloured balls.

clue.text: Body part covered by prisoner's sunglasses?

indicators.note: something covered is wrapped on all sides, so it goes inside

parts.note: a con is a convict; con's
the lip is part of the body

explanation.surface: An inmate's shades hide part of his face.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip-ons are tinted lenses that attach over ordinary glasses, sunglasses of a sort, hence the query.

clue.text: Moist, like seafood?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: resembling a shellfish

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is invented for fun: the suffix -MY can mean 'like', so CLAM plus MY reads as resembling a clam.
explanation.definitionFit: Clammy describes unpleasantly damp, sticky skin or air, and splits as clam plus -my.

clue.text: God's personal assistant getting very upset

indicators.note: to get something is to take it in, so these letters close around the other
in a down entry, upset means turned up, so read bottom to top

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so tired'

explanation.surface: A deity's PA is extremely distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is'. Personal assistant suggests PA, but it is the phone's voice helper, wrapped in reversed SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian deity of the dead and the afterlife.

clue.text: I can still stray a little bit

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off course, so the letters drift out of order

explanation.surface: Someone admits they can still wander off a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark, as in 'not a scintilla of evidence'.

clue.text: Cut husband out to be economical

indicators.note: the letter is taken out and dropped

parts.note: a shave is a cut of the hair

explanation.surface: Drop the husband from the budget in order to economise.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut out the husband looks like one instruction; Cut is SHAVE and 'out' removes the H.
explanation.definitionFit: To save is to spend less and put money aside, which is being economical.

clue.text: Commotion unduly restricts director

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the outer word holds the letter inside

explanation.surface: An overbearing film shoot where too much fuss hems in the director.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or kerfuffle, a commotion.

clue.text: Object of night out …

indicators.note: a word that is out is disordered, so its letters rearrange

explanation.surface: Run on with the next clue, it reads as the aim of a night on the town being sex, in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 28 for the surface only; each clue is solved on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any object, item or article.

clue.text: Former Welsh footballer's picked up engagements

indicators.note: picking something up on a radio means hearing it, so it is how the name sounds

parts.note: Ryan Giggs, the Manchester United and Wales winger

explanation.surface: A retired Welsh player has taken on some bookings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigs are booked performances, especially for musicians: paid engagements.

clue.text: … in Rome: sex and food?

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, and six in Roman numerals is VI

explanation.surface: Continuing 26: a Roman night out offers sex and a good meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Sex looks like the obvious English word, but in Rome it is the Latin number six.
explanation.definitionFit: Viand is an old, formal word for an item of food.

clue.text: Bankers heading off to inform the authorities, doubtless

indicators.note: with the head taken off, the first letter goes

parts.note: the Gnomes of Zurich, a nickname for Swiss bankers
criminals' slang for telling the police

explanation.surface: Financiers set off to tip off the police, surely.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No messing' is an informal phrase meaning seriously, honestly, without a doubt.
